items.title: Single-species elastic Boltzmann model
items.physical_scope: Adopted nonrelativistic, single-species, monatomic kinetic model in a three-dimensional periodic cell with elastic binary collision data and an incoming-pair factorization. Dilute-gas applicability is qualitative; no density threshold, hard-sphere or Boltzmann–Grad limit, many-particle derivation, existence assertion, or empirical validity is claimed.
items.statement:
Let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(0,L_j)$, with $L_j>0$ measured in metres and opposite faces identified, and let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval measured in seconds. The primitive state variable $f$ is a one-particle number-density field $f:I\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$, measurable for the product Lebesgue sigma-algebra and periodic in $x$, where $x$ is in metres and velocity $v$ is in metres per second; $f\,d^3x\,d^3v$ counts particles, so $f$ has units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$. For solutions, require $f$ and its weak time and spatial derivatives $\partial_t f$ and $\nabla_x f$ to be represented locally by integrable functions, so $f$, $\partial_t f$, and $v\cdot\nabla_x f$ are integrable on every compact subset of the product domain. Only translational kinetic energy $m|v|^2/2$ is modeled; no internal molecular modes are included. The single-particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms and Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin are primitive fixed parameters of this formulation; neither is derived from the collision equation.

An elastic collision quadruple is $(v,w,v',w')\in(\mathbb R^3)^4$ satisfying $v+w=v'+w'$ and $|v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2$; write $Q_{\rm el}$ for this closed set and give it the Borel sets inherited from $(\mathbb R^3)^4$. A collision-rate measure is a function $\nu$ on those sets with $\nu(\varnothing)=0$, values in $[0,\infty]$, and $\nu(\bigcup_n E_n)=\sum_n\nu(E_n)$ for pairwise disjoint measurable $E_n$. This nonnegative countably additive $\nu$ is a primitive collision-rate input, invariant under each particle swap and under interchanging incoming and outgoing pairs, with rate normalization chosen so the collision operator has units of $f$ per second. For the collision equation, restrict each velocity section $f(x,\cdot,t)$ to the collision domain $\mathcal D_\nu$ of positive finite-valued measurable densities; a nonnegative ambient state outside $\mathcal D_\nu$ is not assigned a collision operator by this postulate.

Adopt one-sided incoming molecular chaos: at each collision point and time, the incoming two-particle velocity density used by the collision term is $f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$. No outgoing-pair factorization is adopted, and no derivation from reversible many-particle mechanics or propagation of chaos is asserted.

For $A=f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$ and $B=f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t)$, adopt a collision operator $Q_\nu(f)$, with a jointly measurable locally integrable representative, whose weak action for every compact smooth velocity test and every moment or logarithmic test for which both sides converge absolutely is

$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\psi(v)Q_\nu(f)(x,v,t)\,d^3v=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(B-A)\bigl(\psi(v)+\psi(w)-\psi(v')-\psi(w')\bigr)\,d\nu.$$

The adopted kinetic equation is

$$\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_x f=Q_\nu(f)$$

as an equality of locally integrable functions almost everywhere. These equations and the incoming factorization are physical model postulates, not deductions. This item asserts no empirical measurement, universal dilute-gas threshold, or solution existence.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 8
references.locator: Section III.D, printed pp. 49–54; the incoming molecular-chaos closure and its correlation limitation.

references.title: David Tong, Lectures on Kinetic Theory, Chapter 2
references.locator: Sections 2.2–2.2.3; collision closure and detailed balance. Tong factorizes both pre-collision and post-collision pairs, so this treatment does not support the one-sided incoming factorization adopted here.

items.title: Kinetic number, mass and thermal observables
items.physical_scope: SI definitions for the single-species, three-dimensional, translational kinetic model on states with positive number density and, when temperature is used, positive centered second moment. No isotropy or empirical equation of state is assumed by the definitions.
items.statement:
Work in three spatial and velocity dimensions, with $x$ in metres, $v$ in metres per second, and a nonnegative measurable one-particle number density $f(x,v,t)$ as defined by the kinetic-density model. Adopt Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in that definition, and put $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$. Assume $\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3(v)f(x,v,t)\,d^3v<\infty$ at the state under consideration. Use the primitive fixed particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms and Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin from the adopted Boltzmann model. The number density, mass density, mean velocity, peculiar velocity, translational temperature, stress, heat flux, and energy below are derived moment quantities. Where $n(x,t)>0$, define the number density, mass density, mean velocity, peculiar velocity, and translational temperature by

$$n(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\,d^3v,\qquad \rho(x,t)=m n(x,t),\qquad u(x,t)=\frac1{n(x,t)}\int_{\mathbb R^3}v f\,d^3v,\qquad c(x,v,t)=v-u(x,t),$$

$$T(x,t)=\frac{m}{3k_B n(x,t)}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|v-u(x,t)|^2 f(x,v,t)\,d^3v.$$

Use $u$ only where $n>0$, and use $T$ in the positive-temperature branch only where the centered second moment is strictly positive. Define the kinetic stress tensor, heat-flux vector, and total kinetic-energy density by

$$P(x,t)=m\int_{\mathbb R^3}c\otimes c\,f\,d^3v,\qquad q(x,t)=\frac m2\int_{\mathbb R^3}|c|^2c\,f\,d^3v,\qquad E(x,t)=\frac m2\int_{\mathbb R^3}|v|^2f\,d^3v.$$

Here $n$ is in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $\rho$ in $\mathrm{kg\,m^{-3}}$, $u$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $T$ in kelvins, $P$ in pascals, $q$ in $\mathrm{W\,m^{-2}}$, and $E$ in $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$. The definitions impose no isotropy on $P$; $p$ will denote a separate scalar pressure only in a specified local-equilibrium conclusion.

Let $f_{\rm ref}>0$ be a constant reference density with the same units as $f$. At $f=0$, define both $f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})$ and $f|\log(f/f_{\rm ref})|$ to be zero, their continuous extensions from $f>0$; their products with $v$ or $|v|$ are also zero there. Where both $\int f|\log(f/f_{\rm ref})|\,d^3v$ and $\int |v|f|\log(f/f_{\rm ref})|\,d^3v$ are finite, define the dimensionless-log kinetic entropy integral, its flux, the physical kinetic entropy density, and its flux by

$$h=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v,\qquad J_H=\int_{\mathbb R^3}v f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v,\qquad s_{\rm kin}=-k_Bh,\qquad j_{\rm kin}=-k_BJ_H.$$

Thus $h$ and $J_H$ have units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ and $\mathrm{m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$, respectively; $s_{\rm kin}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$ and $j_{\rm kin}$ has units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$. These are kinetic-model observables; $s_{\rm kin}$ is not the fine-grained Gibbs entropy of a reversible many-particle state.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 10
references.locator: Section III.G, printed pp. 64–67; collision moments, pressure tensor, internal kinetic energy, and heat flux.

references.title: David Tong, Lectures on Kinetic Theory, Chapter 2
references.locator: Sections 2.4.1–2.4.2, printed pp. 35–42; number density, mass density, mean velocity, pressure tensor, and ideal-fluid moments.

items.title: Local kinetic H balance for the elastic Boltzmann model
items.physical_scope: Conditional pointwise local kinetic H balance for positive regular solutions of the adopted single-species elastic Boltzmann model, under explicit velocity envelopes and absolutely convergent logarithmic collision tests. This is a model deduction, not a many-particle theorem or empirical claim.
items.statement:
Let $I\subseteq\mathbb R$ be an open time interval in seconds and let
$\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$ be a periodic spatial cell with
$L_j>0$ in metres. Let $v\in\mathbb R^3$ be measured in metres per second and
let $f:I\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to(0,\infty)$ be measurable, continuously
differentiable in $(t,x)$, and twice continuously differentiable in $v$.
Assume $f\,d^3x\,d^3v$ counts particles, so $f$ has units
$\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$. Put
$Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in(\mathbb R^3)^4:v+w=v'+w',\quad |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$, with its relative Borel sigma-algebra, and
let $\nu$ be the nonnegative symmetric collision-rate measure on $Q_{\rm el}$
in the adopted model. Fix a constant $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as
$f$, and put $\ell=\log(f/f_{\rm ref})$, which is dimensionless,
$A=f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$, and $B=f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t)$. Let
$v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and
$\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$.

For every compact time interval $J\subset I$, assume there are integrable
velocity majorants, independent of $(x,t)\in\Omega\times J$, for each of
$f\omega_3(v)$, $f|\ell|$, $|v|f|\ell|$,
$(1+|\ell|)|\partial_t f|$, and
$(1+|\ell|)|v|\,|\nabla_x f|$. At every $(x,t)$, assume that $f(x,\cdot,t)$
belongs to the collision domain and that the weak collision tests $1$ and
$\ell(x,\cdot,t)$ are measurable and absolutely convergent. For each $t\in I$,
assume that the map
$$x\longmapsto\int_{Q_{\rm el}}|(A-B)\log(A/B)|\,d\nu$$
is measurable and belongs to $L^1(\Omega,dx)$. Assume that $f$ solves the adopted kinetic equation
$\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_x f=Q_\nu(f)$ for Lebesgue-almost every velocity at every fixed $(x,t)$. This sectionwise solution sense is an additional hypothesis for the pointwise balance below.

Define
$$h(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v,\qquad J_H(x,t)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}v f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v,$$
where $h$ and $J_H$ have units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ and
$\mathrm{m^{-2}\,s^{-1}}$, respectively.
Also define
$$D(x,t)=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)\log(A/B)\,d\nu.$$
Under the collision-rate normalization in the adopted model, $D$ has units
$\mathrm{m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$.
Then $D(x,t)\ge0$ and
$$\partial_t h+\nabla_x\cdot J_H=-D$$
throughout $I\times\Omega$. The identity is conditional on the adopted weak
collision model and makes no assertion about reversible many-particle entropy
or empirical validity.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 9
references.locator: Section III.E, printed pp. 56–57; local H balance, collision symmetrization and the entropy-production sign.

references.title: David Tong, Lectures on Kinetic Theory, Chapter 2
references.locator: Section 2.3, printed pp. 32–35; local entropy balance and the H-theorem sign mechanism.

items.title: Entropy production in the adopted collision model
items.physical_scope: Conditional local and periodic-global kinetic-entropy balance for positive regular solutions of the adopted d=3 elastic Boltzmann model, under the stated moment, logarithmic-test, flux, and differentiation integrability hypotheses. This is not a theorem about fine-grained Hamiltonian Gibbs entropy or empirical validity of the model.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every $\mathbb N$-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$ be a periodic cell with $L_j>0$ in metres, and let $I$ be an open time interval in seconds. Let $f:I\times\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\to(0,\infty)$ be periodic, continuously differentiable in $t,x$, and twice continuously differentiable in $v$, with $v$ in metres per second and $f$ in $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$. Fix $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$, and a constant $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as $f$; put $\ell=\log(f/f_{\rm ref})$. On each compact time interval, assume integrable velocity majorants uniform in $x,t$ for each of $f\omega_3$, $f|\ell|$, $|v|f|\ell|$, $(1+|\ell|)|\partial_t f|$, and $(1+|\ell|)|v|\,|\nabla_x f|$. Define the elastic collision set

$$Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in(\mathbb R^3)^4:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$$

with its relative Borel sigma-algebra, and let $\nu$ be the nonnegative symmetric collision-rate measure on $Q_{\rm el}$. At every $(x,t)$ assume $f(x,\cdot,t)$ belongs to the collision domain and the weak identity

$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\psi(v)Q_\nu(f)(x,v,t)\,d^3v=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(B-A)\bigl(\psi(v)+\psi(w)-\psi(v')-\psi(w')\bigr)\,d\nu$$

holds absolutely for $\psi=1$ and $\psi=\ell(x,\cdot,t)$, where $A=f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t)$ and $B=f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t)$. For each $t\in I$, assume that the map
$$x\longmapsto\int_{Q_{\rm el}}|(A-B)\log(A/B)|\,d\nu$$
is measurable and belongs to $L^1(\Omega,dx)$. Assume that $f$ solves $\partial_t f+v\cdot\nabla_x f=Q_\nu(f)$ for Lebesgue-almost every velocity at every fixed $(x,t)$. This sectionwise equality is an additional solution hypothesis beyond the adopted product-almost-everywhere equation.

$$A(x,v,w,t)=f(x,v,t)f(x,w,t),\qquad B(x,v',w',t)=f(x,v',t)f(x,w',t).$$

Define

$$D(x,t)=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(A-B)\log(A/B)\,d\nu.$$
Under the adopted collision-rate normalization, $D$ has units
$\mathrm{m^{-3}\,s^{-1}}$.

Then $D(x,t)\ge0$, and the physical kinetic entropy density and flux $s_{\rm kin}=-k_B\int f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v$ and $j_{\rm kin}=-k_B\int v f\log(f/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v$ satisfy

$$\partial_t s_{\rm kin}+\nabla_x\cdot j_{\rm kin}=k_BD\ge0.$$

Here $s_{\rm kin}$ and $j_{\rm kin}$ have units $\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}\,K^{-1}}$
and $\mathrm{J\,m^{-2}\,s^{-1}\,K^{-1}}$, respectively.

Consequently, on the periodic cell, $\mathcal S_{\rm kin}(t)=\int_\Omega s_{\rm kin}(x,t)\,d^3x$ has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}}$ and is nondecreasing. Its rate has units $\mathrm{J\,K^{-1}\,s^{-1}}$. This is a conditional deduction of the adopted collision model; it does not assert increase of fine-grained Hamiltonian Gibbs entropy or that the model describes nature.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 9
references.locator: Section III.E, printed pp. 56–57; complete H-theorem symmetrization and sign argument.

references.title: David Tong, Lectures on Kinetic Theory, Chapter 2
references.locator: Section 2.3, printed pp. 32–35; Boltzmann H-theorem derivation and its molecular-chaos premise.

items.title: Conditional ideal-gas Euler kinetic interface
items.physical_scope: Conditional d=3, periodic, monatomic Boltzmann-to-Euler interface under the exact dimensionless fast-collision equation, C1 positive limiting fields, and strong weighted-L1 convergence of the kinetic density to its local Maxwellian, including the stated initial convergence. No existence or convergence theorem, Navier–Stokes limit, or empirical derivation is claimed.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every $\mathbb N$-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $\Omega=\prod_{j=1}^3(\mathbb R/L_j\mathbb Z)$ be a fixed rectangular periodic cell with periods $L_j>0$ in metres, $T_*>0$ in seconds, and $\varepsilon>0$ a dimensionless fast-collision parameter. Spatial position $x$ is measured in metres, velocity $v$ in metres per second, and $f^\varepsilon d^3x\,d^3v$ counts particles, so $f^\varepsilon$ has units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$. Put $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\omega_k(v)=\sum_{j=0}^k(|v|/v_*)^j$ for $k=2,3$. For each $\varepsilon$, let $f^\varepsilon>0$ be periodic on $\Omega$, continuously differentiable in $t,x$, and twice continuously differentiable in $v$ on $\Omega\times\mathbb R^3\times[0,T_*]$. Let $f_{\rm ref}>0$ be constant in the same units as $f^\varepsilon$ and put $\ell^\varepsilon=\log(f^\varepsilon/f_{\rm ref})$. On each compact time interval, require integrable velocity majorants uniform in $x,t$ for each of $\omega_3 f^\varepsilon$, $\omega_3|\partial_t f^\varepsilon|$, $\omega_3|v\cdot\nabla_xf^\varepsilon|$, $f^\varepsilon|\ell^\varepsilon|$, $|v|f^\varepsilon|\ell^\varepsilon|$, $(1+|\ell^\varepsilon|)|\partial_t f^\varepsilon|$, and $(1+|\ell^\varepsilon|)|v||\nabla_x f^\varepsilon|$. Require the collision logarithmic test to be absolutely integrable. Define

$$Q_{\rm el}=\{(v,w,v',w')\in(\mathbb R^3)^4:v+w=v'+w',\ |v|^2+|w|^2=|v'|^2+|w'|^2\}$$

with its relative Borel sigma-algebra and let $\nu$ be the nonnegative symmetric collision-rate measure on this set. For each admissible velocity test $\psi$ with absolute convergence, the collision operator is assumed to satisfy

$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\psi(v)Q_\nu(f^\varepsilon)(x,v,t)\,d^3v=\frac14\int_{Q_{\rm el}}(B-A)\bigl(\psi(v)+\psi(w)-\psi(v')-\psi(w')\bigr)\,d\nu,$$

where $A=f^\varepsilon(x,v,t)f^\varepsilon(x,w,t)$ and $B=f^\varepsilon(x,v',t)f^\varepsilon(x,w',t)$. In particular require this identity for $\psi=1,mv_i,m|v|^2/2$; the elastic collision constraints make each corresponding collision bracket zero. Require $f^\varepsilon$ to solve

$$\varepsilon\bigl(\partial_t f^\varepsilon+v\cdot\nabla_x f^\varepsilon\bigr)=Q_\nu(f^\varepsilon),$$

Let $m>0$ in kilograms and $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin. Let $n,u,T$ be $C^1$ periodic fields, with $n,T$ bounded above and bounded away from zero and $u$ bounded, and define their local Maxwellian by

$$M_{n,u,T}(v)=n\left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_BT}\right)^{3/2}\exp\left(-\frac{m|v-u|^2}{2k_BT}\right),$$

where $n$ is number density in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, $u$ is velocity in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, $T$ is translational temperature in kelvins, $p$ is pressure in pascals ($\mathrm{J\,m^{-3}}$), and $I_3$ below is the identity tensor on $\mathbb R^3$.

For the fixed velocity unit $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, assume

$$\int_0^{T_*}\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3(v)|f^\varepsilon-M_{n,u,T}|\,d^3v\,d^3x\,dt\longrightarrow0\quad\text{as }\varepsilon\to0,$$

and assume the initial convergence

$$\int_\Omega\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_2(v)|f^\varepsilon(x,v,0)-M_{n(x,0),u(x,0),T(x,0)}(v)|\,d^3v\,d^3x\longrightarrow0.$$

Then, with $\rho=mn$, $E=\frac12\rho|u|^2+\frac32nk_BT$, and local-equilibrium scalar pressure $p=nk_BT$, the limiting fields satisfy the compressible ideal-monatomic-gas Euler equations

$$\partial_t\rho+\nabla_x\cdot(\rho u)=0,$$

$$\partial_t(\rho u)+\nabla_x\cdot(\rho u\otimes u+pI_3)=0,$$

$$\partial_tE+\nabla_x\cdot((E+p)u)=0.$$

The equations hold distributionally and pointwise because the limiting fields are $C^1$; the initial trace is the one supplied by the initial convergence. The weighted strong convergence is a hypothesis, not a consequence of small $\varepsilon$, the entropy estimate, or the adopted model alone. This is a conditional model deduction, not an empirical claim.

references.title: Mehran Kardar, MIT OpenCourseWare 8.333, Statistical Mechanics I, Lecture 11
references.locator: Section III.H, printed pp. 67–68; local Maxwellian moments and zeroth-order fluid equations.

references.title: David Tong, Lectures on Kinetic Theory, Chapter 2
references.locator: Section 2.4.2, printed pp. 41–43; local Maxwellian, ideal-gas pressure, and Euler reduction, with the streaming-equation qualification.

items.title: Conserving homogeneous BGK idealization
items.physical_scope: Separately adopted, spatially homogeneous, single-species, monatomic BGK relaxation model with positive translational temperature, constant phenomenological relaxation time, and a dimensionless fast-collision scale. It is not the binary Boltzmann collision operator, an inhomogeneous hydrodynamic limit, a many-particle derivation, or an empirical claim.
items.statement:
Adopt Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$ as in the BGK definition: for every family $(X_j)_{j\in\mathbb N}$ of nonempty sets there is a function $a$ with domain $\mathbb N$ such that $a(j)\in X_j$ for every $j\in\mathbb N$.

Let $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and $\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$. A velocity density $g:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ is admissible when it is finite-valued and Lebesgue measurable, $g\,d^3v$ is a number density in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ (so $g$ has units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$), and
$$\int_{\mathbb R^3}\omega_3(v)g(v)\,d^3v<\infty.$$
The primitive parameters are species mass $m>0$ in kilograms and Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin. For an admissible $g$ with $n[g]:=\int_{\mathbb R^3}g\,d^3v>0$ and positive centered second moment, define
$$u[g]:=\frac{1}{n[g]}\int_{\mathbb R^3}v g(v)\,d^3v,\qquad T[g]:=\frac{m}{3k_Bn[g]}\int_{\mathbb R^3}|v-u[g]|^2g(v)\,d^3v.$$
The domain condition ensures $T[g]>0$.
Define its moment-matched Maxwellian by
$$M[g](v)=n[g]\left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_BT[g]}\right)^{3/2}\exp\left(-\frac{m|v-u[g]|^2}{2k_BT[g]}\right).$$
It has the same number, momentum, and kinetic-energy moments as $g$. For a constant relaxation time $\tau>0$ in seconds, adopt the homogeneous collision model
$$Q_{\rm BGK}(g)=\frac{M[g]-g}{\tau}.$$

Let $f_0$ be an admissible initial density with positive number density and positive centered second moment. For each dimensionless $\varepsilon>0$, a trajectory considered in the accelerated model is a continuously differentiable map
$$f^\varepsilon\in C^1\!\left([0,\infty);L^1\!\left(\mathbb R^3,\omega_3(v)\,d^3v\right)\right),$$
whose states have nonnegative admissible representatives with positive number density and positive centered second moment at every $t\ge0$, and whose initial trace satisfies $f^\varepsilon(0)=f_0$ in this weighted $L^1$ space. The derivative is the Banach-space derivative, with the right derivative at $t=0$. Adopt
$$\frac{d}{dt}f^\varepsilon(t)=\frac{M[f^\varepsilon(t)]-f^\varepsilon(t)}{\varepsilon\tau},\qquad t\ge0,$$
as an equality in $L^1(\mathbb R^3,\omega_3(v)\,d^3v)$ at every $t\ge0$.

The model also permits pointwise solution representatives $\widetilde f:\mathbb R^3\times[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ that are jointly measurable, have finite $\omega_3$-weighted velocity integral at every time, and satisfy $\widetilde f(v,0)=f_0(v)$ for almost every $v$. Require their velocity sections to be continuous on $[0,\infty)$ and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ for almost every $v$, with positive number density and centered second moment at every time. In this solution sense, require one full-measure set of velocities on which
$$\partial_t\widetilde f(v,t)=\frac{M[\widetilde f(\cdot,t)](v)-\widetilde f(v,t)}{\varepsilon\tau}$$
holds for every $t>0$, and require on each compact time interval a velocity-integrable majorant for $\omega_3(v)|\partial_t\widetilde f(v,t)|$ independent of $t$. The Banach-space and pointwise equalities specify two solution senses for the same adopted model; neither asserts solution existence. This is a separate phenomenological relaxation model. It does not replace or follow from the binary Boltzmann postulate, and the relaxation-time form is not asserted to be an exact microscopic collision operator. No empirical premise or measured relaxation time is asserted.

references.title: François Golse and C. David Levermore, Fluid Dynamics from Kinetic Equations
references.locator: Lecture 2, section V, 'The BGK Operator', PDF p. 28; local Maxwellian relaxation with positive relaxation time.

references.title: David Tong, Lectures on Kinetic Theory, Chapter 2
references.locator: Section 2.5.1, printed pp. 45–46; the relaxation-time approximation and its explicit non-exactness qualification.

items.title: Exact equilibrium approach in the BGK model
items.physical_scope: Conditional exact homogeneous fast-relaxation branch of the separately adopted single-species BGK model, for nonnegative initial velocity densities with finite dimensionless third-moment weight, positive number density and centered second moment, finite reference-relative entropy, and the stated pointwise solution regularity. It is a model prediction, not a binary-Boltzmann theorem, an inhomogeneous Euler limit, or an empirical claim.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every $\mathbb N$-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function. Let $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$ and
$\omega_3(v)=\sum_{j=0}^3(|v|/v_*)^j$. Let
$f_0:\mathbb R^3\to[0,\infty)$ be a measurable velocity number density,
with $f_0$ in $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$ and $f_0\,d^3v$ measured in
$\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, satisfying
$\int\omega_3 f_0\,d^3v<\infty$, number density
$n_0=\int f_0\,d^3v>0$, positive centered second moment, and finite
reference-relative entropy $\int f_0|\log(f_0/f_{\rm ref})|\,d^3v$, where
$f_{\rm ref}>0$ is constant in the same units as $f_0$. Take the primitive
particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms and Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per
kelvin. Define $u_0=n_0^{-1}\int v f_0\,d^3v$ and
$T_0=m(3k_Bn_0)^{-1}\int |v-u_0|^2f_0\,d^3v>0$. For any nonnegative velocity
density $g$ with finite $\omega_3$ moment, number density
$n[g]=\int g\,d^3v>0$, and positive centered second moment, define
$u[g]=n[g]^{-1}\int vg\,d^3v$,
$T[g]=m(3k_Bn[g])^{-1}\int|v-u[g]|^2g\,d^3v$, and its normalized
moment-matched Maxwellian

$$M[g](v)=n[g]\left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_BT[g]}\right)^{3/2}\exp\left(-\frac{m|v-u[g]|^2}{2k_BT[g]}\right).$$

Write $M=M[f_0]$; it has the same number, momentum, and kinetic-energy
moments as $f_0$.
For $\tau>0$ in seconds and dimensionless $\varepsilon>0$, consider the
homogeneous equation

$$\partial_t f^\varepsilon(v,t)=\frac{M[f^\varepsilon](v,t)-f^\varepsilon(v,t)}{\varepsilon\tau},\qquad f^\varepsilon(v,0)=f_0(v),\quad t\ge0.$$

There is a nonnegative solution
$f^\varepsilon\in C^1([0,\infty);L^1(\omega_3\,d^3v))$ given by

$$f^\varepsilon(v,t)=M(v)+e^{-t/(\varepsilon\tau)}(f_0(v)-M(v)).$$

It solves the equation in $L^1(\omega_3\,d^3v)$ and preserves the number,
momentum, and kinetic-energy moments of $f_0$. It is also the unique solution
in the following pointwise class: a jointly measurable
$\tilde f:\mathbb R^3\times[0,\infty)\to[0,\infty)$ with finite
$\omega_3$-weighted velocity integral at every time and initial trace
$\tilde f(v,0)=f_0(v)$ for almost every $v$, whose velocity sections are
continuous on $[0,\infty)$ and differentiable on $(0,\infty)$ for almost
every $v$. Require a common full-measure set of velocities on which the
equation holds for every $t>0$, and, on each compact time interval, an
integrable $\omega_3$-weighted majorant for $\partial_t\tilde f$ independent
of $t$. Also require the density and temperature of $\tilde f$ to remain
positive. These envelopes permit differentiation of the three moment
integrals and justify the conservation argument in the proof.

For each $T_*>0$, with the dimensionless fixed velocity weight
$\|g\|_{1,3}=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1+|v/v_*|^3)|g(v)|\,d^3v$, which has
units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ for velocity densities $g$, it satisfies

$$\|f^\varepsilon(t)-M\|_{1,3}=e^{-t/(\varepsilon\tau)}\|f_0-M\|_{1,3},\qquad \int_0^{T_*}\|f^\varepsilon(t)-M\|_{1,3}\,dt\le\varepsilon\tau\|f_0-M\|_{1,3}.$$

Writing $H(g)=\int_{\mathbb R^3}g\log(g/f_{\rm ref})\,d^3v$ with $0\log0:=0$,
which has units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$ for velocity densities $g$, the entropy
gap obeys

$$0\le H(f^\varepsilon(t))-H(M)\le e^{-t/(\varepsilon\tau)}\bigl(H(f_0)-H(M)\bigr).$$

Thus for each fixed $t>0$, $f^\varepsilon(t)\to M$ in this weighted $L^1$
norm as $\varepsilon\to0$, while $f^\varepsilon(0)=f_0$; if $f_0$ differs
from $M$ on a set of positive measure, the initial mismatch is nonzero. If
$f_0=M$ almost everywhere, the formula gives the stationary equilibrium with
zero norm and entropy gaps. This is an exact homogeneous BGK model prediction
and does not assert an inhomogeneous Boltzmann-to-Euler limit or an observed
relaxation.

items.title: Prepared non-Maxwellian distribution and initial layer
items.physical_scope: Hypothetical spatially homogeneous preparation for the single-species BGK model, using a compactly supported non-Maxwellian initial velocity density. No apparatus, observation, or empirical relaxation is reported.
items.statement:
Assume Countable Choice $\mathrm{AC}_\omega$: every $\mathbb N$-indexed family of nonempty sets has a choice function.

Consider a hypothetical homogeneous three-dimensional gas with particle mass $m>0$ in kilograms, Boltzmann constant $k_B>0$ in joules per kelvin, number density $n_0>0$ in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$, translational temperature $T_0>0$ in kelvins, and a constant reference density $f_{\rm ref}>0$ with the same units as the velocity density below. Put $\theta=k_BT_0/m$ in $\mathrm{m^2\,s^{-2}}$, $V_c=\sqrt{3\theta}$ in $\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$, and define the prepared number density in velocity space by

$$f_0(v)=\frac{n_0}{8V_c^3}\,\mathbf 1_{[-V_c,V_c]^3}(v),\qquad v\in\mathbb R^3.$$

The density $f_0$ has units $\mathrm{s^3\,m^{-6}}$, so $f_0\,d^3v$ is a number density in $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$.

Here $\mathbf 1_C$ is the function equal to one on the cube $C$ and zero outside it. The corresponding Maxwellian with the same number density, zero mean velocity, and temperature $T_0$ is

$$M(v)=n_0\left(\frac{m}{2\pi k_BT_0}\right)^{3/2}\exp\left(-\frac{m|v|^2}{2k_BT_0}\right).$$

Define the dimensionless weighted norm by $\|g\|_{1,3}=\int_{\mathbb R^3}(1+|v/v_*|^3)|g(v)|\,d^3v$, where $v_*=1\,\mathrm{m\,s^{-1}}$; for velocity densities $g$ it has units $\mathrm{m^{-3}}$. Under the homogeneous fast-scale conserving BGK model with $\tau>0$ seconds and dimensionless $\varepsilon>0$, this preparation has an exact initial-layer solution: for every fixed $t>0$, $f^\varepsilon(t)\to M$ in this weighted $L^1$ norm as $\varepsilon\to0$, while $f^\varepsilon(0)=f_0\ne M$. The compactly supported $f_0$ is a hypothetical distribution, not an observed preparation or experiment.
